nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a type of configurations, $R$ an additive commutative group, $\Phi : S \to R$ a potential, $s_0, s_1, s_2, \dots$ a run of configurations and $t_0, t_1, \dots \in R$ the actual costs of its operations, operation $i$ taking $s_i$ to $s_{i+1}$. The amortized cost of operation $i$ is The actual cost $t_i$ is whatever the client's cost model counts (rotations, pointer changes, unit-cost steps); nothing here…
nodes.title: Amortized cost of an operation

nodes.summary: For every potential $\Phi$, run $s_0, s_1, \dots$ and actual costs $t_0, t_1, \dots$, with amortized costs $a_i = t_i + \Phi(s_{i+1}) - \Phi(s_i)$, and for every $m \ge 0$, The total actual cost equals the total amortized cost plus the net decrease in potential from the initial to the final configuration. The proof is the telescoping of the potential terms.
nodes.title: Potential method: telescoping identity

nodes.summary: If $a_i \le c_i$ for every $i < m$, then This is the form in which an amortized bound for each operation becomes a bound on the total time of a sequence: one adds the per-operation bounds and the net potential drop. Sleator and Tarjan derive their balance, static-optimality, static-finger and working-set theorems for splay trees this way from the access lemma.
nodes.title: Potential method with per-operation amortized bounds

nodes.summary: If $\Phi(s_0) = 0$ and $\Phi(s_i) \ge 0$ for every $i$, then for every $m$ This is the situation Tarjan singles out as the common one ("the initial potential is zero and the potential is always nonnegative"); it corresponds to the banker's view of amortization in which credits are never borrowed. For instance, a stack whose potential is its size starts at zero, and an operation popping $k$ items and pushing one has…
nodes.title: Potential method with a nonnegative potential that starts at zero

nodes.summary: Let the costs and potentials take values in an ordered additive commutative group. If $\Phi(s_0) \le \Phi(s_m)$, then that is, the total amortized cost of the first $m$ operations is an upper bound on their total actual cost.
nodes.title: Potential method: amortized costs bound actual costs

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
